threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver shouts ‘next stop’ and it’s not even a stop. Locals just nod and scroll.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and a guy was singing opera on the top deck. Couldn’t tell if he was brilliant or just mad. The driver didn't even blink.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the baker greets you by name and knows your favorite bread, that’s when you know this isn’t just a place you live, it’s home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can find a spontaneous dance party at a bus stop. You'd think it's just the buses, but sometimes, the beats take over.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name at least three taco trucks that don’t have long lines after midnight.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy in a full suit hop on the 38 at Civic Center, grabbed a seat, then pulled out a ukulele. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals hang out at Park Güell, but the real vibe is at Plaça de la Vila, especially during the evening when the kids play and neighbors chat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones staring at the metro map like it's a treasure map, fumbling for the right line even after a month here.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still go to Tesco instead of the local farm shop. That’s a rookie mistake—everyone knows the best greens come from the market, not a chain.
Last night on the 333, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old school garage tunes. Had us all laughing, but the driver was not impressed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the late-night kebab shop ran out of bread and the owner just laughed, offered me a slice of pizza instead. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a public art installation made from old tram parts, right by the Warschauer Brücke – a hidden gem for the curious.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local would know the aroma of fresh tortillas at La Palma can change with the wind. Outsiders just smell the carne asada.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 19 going the wrong way yesterday, ended up listening to a guy in a full tuxedo argue with a busker about jazz improvisation.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the plaça is for lounging, but it's really just a shortcut for locals dodging the crowds on their way to the bakery.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by how they hesitate at the metro ticket machines, still trying to decipher the multiple zones and prices.
